title: Eight-round AES-256 single-key MITM key recovery, low-memory tradeoff

target.description: Eight-round AES-256, rounds 0 through 7 in the authors' indexing, using the actual AES-256 key expansion. The reduced cipher omits the last MixColumns and ends with AddRoundKey; Section 4.1 also explains the equivalent-subkey change if the last MixColumns is retained.

setting.key_relation: One unknown secret AES key; the attacker does not select related keys or obtain related-key oracles.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: chosen-plaintext structures under the same designated secret key
assumptions: The four-round multiset lookup table of Section 3.2 is reused after adding one final attack round.
The source uses 2^81 structures of 2^32 chosen plaintexts and enumerates 2^144 within-structure pairs.
AES-256 key-schedule Proposition 5 supports 2^48 needed-subkey candidates per pair; the output active byte can be anywhere except positions 0, 5, 10 and 15 for the stated cost.
Expected right-pair and multiset-matching counts follow the source's truncated-differential model; no independent implementation is asserted.
Low-memory output-active byte excludes0,5,10,15; low-data variant tests y5with one extra table parameter.

time.note: Section 4.1 reports 2^196 AES-encryption-equivalent time, with 2^48 needed-subkey candidates for each of 2^144 pairs. The cost is the online key-enumeration/multiset-testing estimate, not an independently audited all-stage total.

data.note: Section 4.1 explicitly uses 2^81 structures of 2^32 messages, all encrypted under one unknown key; no chosen-ciphertext or related-key access is used.

memory.note: The unchanged four-round middle lookup table contains about 2^80 multisets, represented by about 2^82 AES blocks. This is the source's table-storage estimate, not a bit count.

preprocessing.note: A precomputed table is mandatory. Section 3.2 prices construction of the reused four-round table at about 2^84 AES encryptions, but Section 4.1 does not independently itemize an extension-specific offline budget; the numerical field is left null instead of re-labelling that estimate as a full eight-round preprocessing total.

success.description: Section4.1 extends the simple attack with2^113 chosen plaintexts and memory2^82, at time2^172 for AES192 or2^196 for AES256. The differential pair is acquired only in expectation; enumerating candidate subkeys and testing the multiset does not quantify joint completed-key success. The separate2^107-data/2^96-memory parallel-differential variant is not this assignment.

review.scope: Source-first review of Figure5, the eight-round enumeration, Propositions3–5 and exact Table1 assignment. Useful-pair acquisition and completed-output error remain unquantified. Distinct key-schedule constraints, budgets and the parallel-differential variant are kept separate. No probability transferred from a local filter or another row; audit gates unchanged.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.4-5, Section 2.1 (round operations, zero-based indexing and cost units); pp.13-15, Section 4.1 and Figure 5; p.8, Table 1, eight-round row with data 2^113 and memory 2^82.
evidence.interpretation: The original construction, not a later survey, reports the AES-256 low-memory point with time 2^196, data 2^113 chosen plaintexts and memory 2^82 128-bit blocks. The derivation uses the real single-key AES-256 schedule. The text supplies no numerical success probability and makes an attack claim rather than a security lower-bound claim.

evidence.locator: PDF p.10, Section 3.2, Precomputation phase; p.13, opening paragraph of Section 4.1.
evidence.interpretation: Section 3.2 gives an approximate 2^84-AES-encryption setup cost for its 2^80-multiset table. Section 4.1 extends that simple attack by adding a last round and retains its 2^82-block table. Reuse is explicit, but the extension's separate offline accounting is not tabulated; the 2^84 context is retained in the note rather than promoted to a separately reported extension-specific total.

evidence.interpretation: Raw-first independent full inventory, original-PDF SHA recheck, bounded official version/successor checks. Existing quoted resource tuple and stableIDpreserved; no author code executed.

evidence.locator: PDF13–15 §4.1 and PDF5 single-key setting; two source differential layouts of the same8round extension.
evidence.interpretation: Source-supported semantic normalization of existing key-relation wording and designated target; no added oracle or key-control assumption.

evidence.interpretation: Targeted success audit: expected counts and conditional correctness are retained without inventing an end-to-end probability or a Poisson independence assumption.

evidence.locator: Author PDF8 Table1; PDF13–15 Section4.1, Figure5, Steps1–4, Propositions3–5,2^113-data/2^82-memory construction and distinct2^107-data/2^96-memory alternative.

limitations: The attack and its enormous multiset table have not been independently implemented or reproduced.
The reported time is tied to the authors' key-testing cost model; extension-specific offline accounting and numerical whole-key success remain unreported.
Active-byte placement restrictions are part of this low-memory design point; the companion low-data variant uses a larger collection of tables.
This record preserves the inspected 2013 source version and is not a claim of current best-known cryptanalysis.
